Unfold the first conjunct into the uniformity formulation of `TendstoUniformlyOnFilter`, then use the metric basis of entourages
\[
\{(x,y)\mid \operatorname{dist}(x,y)<\varepsilon\},\qquad \varepsilon>0.
\]
The source filter is the product filter `p ×ˢ p'`, so this gives exactly the stated eventual ε-distance condition.

For the second conjunct, prove both universally quantified statements independently, making the displayed `Iff` logically immediate.

- For locally uniform convergence of products, work near each `x ∈ s`. Use the local boundedness of `f` and `g` to obtain bounds on the limits and, from locally uniform convergence, eventual bounds on `F i` and `G i`. Then apply boundedness of the scalar action to the usual two-error decomposition of
  \[
  F_i\smul G_i-f\smul g,
  \]
  controlling one factor by a local bound and the other by its locally uniform error. The local boundedness assumptions are essential here.

- For the summability statement, use that unconditional summability of a real family implies summability of its absolute values. Since
  \[
  0\le \operatorname{toNNReal}(f_n)\le |f_n|,
  \]
  comparison gives summability of the nonnegative real family; transfer this to `NNReal` via its norm/coercion into `Real`.

Thus neither direction of the outer `Iff` needs to use its premise: each side follows from a standard, independent convergence or summability principle.
